# PCB Parts MCP Server

> MCP server for electronic component data: a searchable daily snapshot of JLCPCB's in-stock catalog (630K+ parts with stock >= 10), live stock and prices from JLCPCB, Mouser and DigiKey, EasyEDA pinouts and footprints, SamacSys KiCad files, reference board schematics, sensor lookup and PCB design rules.

- Endpoint: `https://pcbparts.dev/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, stateless)
- Auth: none
- Rate limit: 100 requests a minute per IP
- Health: `https://pcbparts.dev/health`
- Source: https://github.com/Averyy/pcbparts-mcp

## Setup

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add -s user --transport http pcbparts https://pcbparts.dev/mcp
```

Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`) and Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`); VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`) uses the key `"servers"` instead of `"mcpServers"`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pcbparts": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://pcbparts.dev/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Clients that only run local commands (Copilot for Xcode): `{"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://pcbparts.dev/mcp"]}`.

## Which tool

- Find parts: `jlc_search`. Confirm stock before ordering, or find parts with stock under 10: `jlc_stock_check`.
- One part's live details: `jlc_get_part(lcsc=...)`. A manufacturer part number to JLCPCB parts: `jlc_get_part(mpn=...)`.
- Replacement for a part: get its LCSC code (from `jlc_get_part(mpn=...)` if needed), then `jlc_find_alternatives(lcsc=...)`.
- Mouser or DigiKey data: `mouser_get_part`, `digikey_get_part`, only when the user wants that distributor.
- Pins and footprint pads: `jlc_get_pinout`. KiCad files: `cse_get_kicad` (slow).
- How real boards wire an IC: `board_search(component=...)`, then `board_get(slug, focus=IC)`.
- Choosing a sensor: `sensor_recommend`. Design guidance: `get_design_rules`.

## Tools

### jlc_search

Searches the daily snapshot (stock >= 10). Stock and the 1-piece price are as of `data_as_of`.

- Arguments: `query` (plain words, e.g. "100nF 25V X7R 0402"), `subcategory_name` or `subcategory_id`, `spec_filters`, `package` or `packages` (OR, max 50), `manufacturer`, `min_stock` (default 10), `library_type` ("basic", "preferred", "no_fee", "extended", "all"), `prefer_no_fee` (default true: basic and preferred first), `pcba_type` ("economic" or "standard_only"), `sort_by` ("stock" by default, "price" or "spec"), `sort_spec`, `sort_order`, `limit` (default 20, max 100), `offset` (max 10000), `strict` (default false), `match_all_terms` (default true).
- `spec_filters`: up to 50 of `{"name", "op", "value"}`, e.g. `[{"name": "Vgs(th)", "op": "<", "value": "2V"}]`. Operators `=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`; `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` work only on numeric specs. Names ignore case. Unitless values use base units (V, A, ohms, F, H, Hz, W, mm, bytes). `jlc_search_help(subcategory=...)` lists a subcategory's specs, which are numeric, and which sort.
- Short spec names: `Vgs(th)`, `Vds`, `Id`, `Rds(on)`, `Vr`, `If`, `Vf`, `Vceo`, `Ic`, `Vout`, `Iout`, `Quiescent Current` (`Iq`), `Supply Voltage`, `Isolation Voltage`, `Capacitance`, `Resistance`, `Inductance`, `Voltage`, `Tolerance`, `Power`, `DCR`, `Isat`, `Frequency`, `Load Capacitance`, `Junction Capacitance`, `Reverse Stand-Off Voltage (Vrwm)`, `Operating Temperature` (°C).
- Sorting by a spec: `sort_spec` (e.g. "RDS(on)@4.5V", "Dropout@500mA", "Vf@1A", "Iq", "Isat") with `sort_order` "asc" (default) or "desc". `sort_order` without `sort_spec`, or `sort_by="spec"` without `sort_spec`, is an error. Parts that don't list the spec come last. Rows add `sort_value` (the figure sorted on); `sort` says what was compared, and `sort.note` says when figures at different test conditions were compared as listed.
- Reply: `total` counts every match before `limit` and `offset`. `filters_applied` lists every filter that ran; `parsed` what the query text gave. `relaxed` names query words, a query-only library preference or a part type left out to get results; `relaxed.dropped_filters` lists parsed spec filters dropped when a part number was retried, so those results don't meet them. `parsed.adjusted_filters` lists specs moved or left out (including a package that fell back to its bare family); `ignored_filters` filters not applied or rarely listed. `unlisted` counts parts a range filter left out only because they list no value. `hint` on an empty reply suggests a next step. `counts_complete=false` means the counts are partial. `valid_values` lists accepted inputs on an error.
- When the search shortens a part number (`LM1117-3.3` searches `LM1117`), `mpn_match` on each result is `full`, `same_suffix` or `family`, in that order.
- MOSFET queries with a gate drive add `rds_on_at_drive`: the RDS(on) listed at or below that drive, or null when none is listed there. Null parts stay in the results.
- `pcba_type="standard_only"` on a part means one such part moves the whole order to Standard assembly. `no_datasheet=true` means JLCPCB lists no datasheet; `no_datasheet_note` clarifies that LCSC or the manufacturer may have one.

### jlc_stock_check

Live JLCPCB search over the whole catalog (7M+ parts). Arguments: `query`, `category_name`/`category_id`, `subcategory_name`/`subcategory_id`, `package`/`packages`, `manufacturer`/`manufacturers` (lists max 50), `library_type`, `min_stock` (default 10; 0 includes out-of-stock), `sort_by` ("quantity" default, "price"), `page` (default 1), `limit` (default 20, max 100). JLCPCB matches whole part numbers and their starts, not text inside them. One LCSC code as `query` returns that part only, with its price tiers.

### jlc_get_part

- `lcsc` (e.g. "C82899"): live details, cached up to an hour.
- `mpn` (e.g. "LM358P"): searches the daily snapshot (stock >= 10) and returns `{mpn, results, total}`; call `jlc_get_part(lcsc=...)` on a result for live stock and full details. It also finds other dash and space spellings, the same maker's packing codes and BOM text with notes ("TL074 OP AMP"), and never a different grade. Inexact matches add `match` (`separators`, `packing`, `alias`, `alternative`, `lcsc`, `related`) and `matched_mpn`; `related` results can be other part types.

Snapshot part rows carry `data_source` (kind, provider, observation time); live lookup observations keep their time through caching. MPN replies include `data_as_of`; misses identify snapshot scope, `availability: unknown_outside_snapshot`, and an optional unexecuted live-check `next_call`.

Reply fields: `prices` (quantity tiers), `datasheet_pdf` (a stable link to the PDF), `datasheet` (LCSC's viewer page, null when none), `maker_datasheet` (the manufacturer's link, where listed), `datasheet_note`, `specs`, `specs_note` (what the listing leaves out for the part type), `spec_evidence` (where reviewed: manufacturer values, conditions, document, printed page, source URL, review date), `spec_discrepancies` (known catalog/document conflicts; catalog specs and numeric filtering/sorting are preserved), `pcba_type`, `lcsc_url`, `has_easyeda_footprint` (null = unknown, false = none). No lifecycle status: use `mouser_get_part` or `digikey_get_part`.

Savings use a rounded legacy $3 Economic loading-fee estimate, labelled with `is_estimate` and `assembly_service_assumption`; confirm current quotes. Standard service differs.

### jlc_get_pinout

`lcsc` or `uuid` (EasyEDA symbol), `footprint` (default false; needs `lcsc`). Pin numbers and names exactly as the EasyEDA symbol has them; numbers match the EasyEDA footprint's pads. `electrical` appears only where the symbol sets it. `unverified` is present when LCSC hasn't verified the symbol. `note`: the pins are named only by number, or a diode/LED-type part whose numbering varies between sources (connect it by pin name). `footprint=true` adds the footprint's name, `source_link`, `pad_count`, `pitch`, `pad_sizes` and `pads` (number, x, y in mm from the origin with y down, shape, size, layer, hole); if the footprint can't be fetched, the pins still come back with `footprint_error`.

Empty `jlc_search` responses can include `why_empty`: tested library/package/stock changes, retained constraints, counts with exact/at_least relation, executable next calls where representable, and `diagnostics_complete`. Only the stock>=10 snapshot is checked. Diagnostics are bounded to three queries/200 ms; incomplete work is explicit and original results remain empty. Negative Vout preserves polarity; impedance@frequency compares that frequency; part-number exclusions are reported as unsupported.

### jlc_find_alternatives

`lcsc` (required LCSC code), `library_type`, `same_package` (default false), `has_easyeda_footprint` (true/false filter), `min_stock` (default 10), `limit` (per list, default 10, max 50), `board_quantity` and `placements_per_board` (default 1, for `comparison.savings`).

- `summary.found` counts `alternatives`: parts whose primary value and required specs match (connector series and contacts, transistor polarity, regulator output and listed input range) and whose readable ratings are the same or better. Ranked basic/preferred first.
- Ratings that are missing or unreadable don't disqualify a part: they're listed in `specs_unparseable`. `unchecked_requirements` lists what wasn't checked; pinout and external circuit always need checking. A regulator's single input rating checks only the maximum.
- `unverified_alternatives` miss a required match or lack comparable rating conditions: compare by hand. Inductor Isat needs comparable inductance-drop criteria and rating bases; thermal current needs matching thermal conditions and bases; DCR needs comparable published bases. Multi-diode current comparisons need loading/thermal evidence. These candidates do not drive the recommended savings comparison.
- `has_easyeda_footprint` checks at most 15 candidates and leaves out any it couldn't check; `summary.footprint_filter` says when.
- Part types without rules return `similar_parts`. RF parts are ordered by `frequency_coverage` of the original's range. Modules and others list the same package and part family first, marked `likely_drop_in` (pinout unchecked).
- Lifecycle (NRND) isn't checked.

### jlc_search_help

No arguments: all categories. `category`: its subcategories. `subcategory`: its filterable specs with type and example values, marked `sort_spec` where sortable.

### mouser_get_part

`part_number`: a Mouser PN or MPN (3-40 characters), or up to 10 joined by "|" ("595-LM358P|NE555P"), one request per call. Matching is loose and returns at most 50 results: use full part numbers when batching and match results by `mfr_part_number`. `not_found` lists numbers with no match. Check `manufacturer`: a number can match another maker's part. `lifecycle` is Mouser's status where it gives one, else null.

### digikey_get_part

`product_number`: one DigiKey PN or full MPN per call (a partial number can find nothing and still uses a request). `part_number`, `price`, `price_breaks` and `min_qty` are one packaging's (the PN given, else the smallest order); `packaging` names it and `other_packaging` lists the rest. `lifecycle` is DigiKey's product status.

### cse_search, cse_get_kicad

SamacSys ComponentSearchEngine; slow: a search takes about 15 s (longer when the service is busy, no fixed limit), and answers are kept. `cse_search(query, limit)` (limit default 5, max 10) says whether KiCad, Eagle or Altium models exist and returns `cse_part_id`. `cse_get_kicad(query or part_id)` returns the `.kicad_sym` and `.kicad_mod` text.

### board_search, board_get

`board_search`: `component` (IC name; adds a cross-board `consensus` when 2+ boards match), `query` (function, e.g. "motor driver"), `tag`, `org`, `layers`, `limit` (default 10, max 50). Unknown tags return `valid_values`. Consensus `pct` divides by `consensus.board_count`.

`board_get`: `slug`, `focus` (IC name, ref like "J1", or value words like "USB-C": returns that part's pin-by-pin neighborhood), `include_bom` (default false; adds plain passives), `include_nets` (default false; full netlist, can be 100 KB+). Components carry the design files' `mpn`, `manufacturer`, `lcsc`, `mouser`, `digikey` where listed. A focused part has `power_pins`, `pin_nets` (each pin's net), `pin_count` and `nc_pins` (pins on no net; `{}` means all connected).

### sensor_recommend

`query`, `measure` (one or a list of up to 20, all must match), `type`, `protocol`, `platform` ("arduino", "esphome", "micropython", "circuitpython", "tasmota", "zephyr", "raspberry_pi"), `limit` (default 15, max 100). Unknown values return `valid_values`. Sorted by how many platforms have drivers. Not for buying: use `jlc_search`.

Sensor capability notes: CCS811 exposes estimated `eco2` and VOC output, with humidity/temperature compensation inputs and operating/stress voltage evidence; these inputs are not selectable direct measurements for that device. Descriptions prefer device/integration sources over breakout marketing.

### get_design_rules

`topic`: empty lists every file; an exact key (`power/ldo`) returns that file; a keyword (`usb`, `type-c`, `lipo`, `stm32g0`) returns matching files.

## How jlc_search reads a query

- Units: `u`/`µ`/`μ` mean micro, `4u7` is 4.7uF (4.7uH for inductors), `6V3` is 6.3V. `10M`/`10Meg` are megaohms, `10m` milliohms. Package `1005` is `0402`.
- A value goes to the spec the part type lists: `5V relay` is the coil voltage, `3.3V LDO` the output, `12V buck` an output range covering 12V, `3.3V level shifter` a supply range covering it, `24V input 3.3V output` both sides of a regulator. A current under 1mA in an LDO/DC-DC query is the quiescent current. A resistance with an ohm unit on MOSFETs, load switches or inductors is a maximum RDS(on) or DCR. If the part type doesn't list the spec, the value is left out and `parsed.adjusted_filters` says so.
- In a MOSFET query, a voltage next to `logic level`, `GPIO` or `MCU` (up to 5V) or `gate`/`Vgs` (up to 20V) is the gate drive; parts with RDS(on) listed at or below it rank first.
- Comparisons in the text keep their operator: `Iq < 10uA`, `Vf < 0.3V`. A sign before a bare value applies to the main rating (`10uF capacitor < 25V`).
- Ranges (supply/output voltage, operating temperature): `=` matches a range that includes the value, `>=` one that reaches it, `<=` one that goes down to it. `-40°C` in a query means rated down to -40°C, `105C` up to 105°C.
- Connectors filter on pin count and pitch where the connector type lists them (`JST PH 2 pin`); `qwiic`/`STEMMA QT` mean 4-pin 1.0mm JST SH, `Grove` 4-pin 2.0mm.
- Packages include their other spellings: `SOT-23` includes `SOT-23-3`, `0603` includes `1608`, a bare `QFN-32` matches VQFN/WQFN/UQFN of any body. `QFN-24-EP(4x4)` keeps the body and exposed pad; if no catalog package has that body, the bare family is matched and `parsed.adjusted_filters` says so (`strict=true` doesn't fall back).
- `basic`, `preferred` and `no fee` in the query set the library filter; `cheapest` sorts by price; `lowest Iq`, `highest Isat`, `most flash` sort by that spec. Arguments win over query words; `library_type="all"` overrides a library word.
- Query words that match nothing together with the rest are left out and named in `relaxed`. With `subcategory_name` or `spec_filters` given, they aren't left out: the reply is empty and `hint` names them. `strict=true` turns off every relaxation and returns an error for unsupported constraints.
- Spec figures are JLCPCB's listings; check datasheets before choosing.

## Library types

| Type | Economic loading fee | Meaning |
|------|--------------|---------|
| `basic` | none | JLCPCB's standard library |
| `preferred` | none | Recommended parts with good availability |
| `extended` | Fee per unique type; calculator uses a rounded $3 estimate | Everything else |
| `no_fee` | none | Filter for basic and preferred together |
| `all` | | No library filter |

## Quotas

Mouser and DigiKey share one key each across all pcbparts.dev users: 1,000 requests a day each (DigiKey's resets at 00:00 UTC), and at most 25 a minute for Mouser and 100 for DigiKey. Batch Mouser lookups, look up one DigiKey part at a time, and don't retry a quota error. Self-hosting with your own keys gives your own limits: https://github.com/Averyy/pcbparts-mcp#self-hosting
